Guides / 07—08

Build palettes by role, not swatch count

Choose surfaces, text, borders and accents, then test the actual touching pairs.

Vijeron · Updated 10 October 2026

Start with content

Choose body text and the main background first. Add secondary surface, button, link, border and state colors only for real needs. Each extra color creates pairs to review in default and interactive states.

Name clear tokens

Names such as text-primary, surface-muted and border-input age better than blue-500 when a hue changes. Keep approved pairs with their HEX values, roles and actual contrast ratios.

Avoid automatic harmony claims

This site's variation tool mixes sRGB channels with white or black to offer five candidates. It is arithmetic, not an aesthetic judgement or accessibility pass. Test each candidate in its role and against its background.

Reproducible example

A compact palette might use one main surface, one body text color, one button accent and one focus color; record text-on-surface and button-label ratios separately.

What to check

Five attractive swatches do not automatically make labels, borders and focus visible.
